answer: A proof-of-stake bond makes each agent identity costly to clone: every voter locks collateral that is slashed on fraud, so one Sybil cannot reuse a single deposit across fake personas. The attacker's cost grows linearly with every invented agent, and rewards vest only at dawn, after the stake has aged, making throwaway identities worthless. Splitting one identity is like a prism dividing a beam—each fragment still needs its own full bond, so flooding the voting ocean demands real capital.
